question.prompt: A data set containing \(20\) numbers, some of which are \(6,\) has mean \(45.\) When all the \(6\)s are removed, the data set has mean \(66.\) How many \(6\)s were in the original data set?

solutions.title: Write an equation for the remaining mean
solutions.explanation:
Removing the \(6\)s changes both the total sum and the number of entries. Let \(k\) be the number of \(6\)s in the original data set.

The original sum is \(20\cdot45=900\). Removing \(k\) copies of \(6\) leaves \(20-k\) numbers with sum \(900-6k\). Since their mean is \(66\),
\[
\frac{900-6k}{20-k}=66.
\]
Multiplying by \(20-k\) and solving gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
900-6k&=66(20-k),\\
900-6k&=1320-66k,\\
60k&=420,\\
k&=7.
\end{aligned}
\]
There were \(\boxed{7}\) copies of \(6\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
